analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, comparing these findings to previously reported data from the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were tested using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women showed increased rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previous national reports but lower than in the private health system, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates across healthcare sectors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform targeted HPV screening strategies, particularly for younger women, and support public health interventions to reduce HPV-related diseases in underserved populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias from single-region data and reliance on self-reported healthcare attendance.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in 39,512 women attending Chile's public health system between 2020-2024. The overall HR-HPV rate was 13.70%, with significantly higher prevalence in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older groups. HPV-positive women showed markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. The prevalence was lower than previously reported in the private health system, suggesting potential healthcare disparities. These findings highlight the need for targeted screening programs, particularly for younger women, and inform public health strategies to reduce HPV-related diseases in underserved populations.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, comparing these findings to previously reported data from the private health system.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cohort study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis_en.methods: Samples were tested using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis_en.main_results: The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women showed increased rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previous national reports but lower than in the private health system, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates across healthcare sectors.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform targeted HPV screening strategies, particularly for younger women, and support public health interventions to reduce HPV-related diseases in underserved populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias from single-region data and reliance on self-reported healthcare attendance.

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

papers.title: Phased amplicon multiplex sequencing for cost-effective detection of high-risk human papillomavirus from cervical samples
papers.abstract: Access to accurate cost-effective technologies for typing high-risk human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) is critical to expand cervical cancer screening and inform vaccination strategies. Compared with clinical-standard quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) assays, HPV genotyping by next-generation sequencing (NGS) provides greater flexibility, scalability, and genotype specificity. We have developed a method for HPV genotyping, HPV Phased Amplicon Multiplex Sequencing (PhAM-Seq), that uses combinatorial barcoding of amplicons with short, variable-length inline sequences to enable higher throughput and lower per-sample costs than conventional amplicon sequencing approaches. We evaluated HPV PhAM-Seq using degenerate and type-specific primers targeting the L1 and E6-E7 gene loci in a blinded cohort of 170 cervical samples previously typed by the Seegene Anyplex II HPV28 Detection qPCR assay. Across eight common hrHPV types (HPV16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 45, 52, and 58), HPV PhAM-Seq demonstrated >80% overall agreement with qPCR using degenerate L1-targeting primers, with the highest sensitivity for HPV16, 31, 33, and 58. Sensitivity for HPV35, 45, and 52 improved to 85% or greater with type-specific primers targeting genes E6/E7. Parallel processing and sequencing enables a single technician to assay hundreds of samples per week at a reagent cost of around $10 USD per sample, with laboratory automation and sequencing on higher-output platforms enabling further scaling and cost reduction to a scale amenable to population-level surveillance. We include a detailed SOP; tools for primer design, sequencing library construction, and sample tracking; and all scripts needed for data analysis to ensure HPV PhAM-Seq can be readily implemented for scalable, cost-effective hrHPV genotyping or extended to other similar applications.

analysis.methods: The method, HPV Phased Amplicon Multiplex Sequencing (PhAM-Seq), uses combinatorial barcoding of amplicons with short, variable-length inline sequences to enable higher throughput and lower per-sample costs than conventional amplicon sequencing approaches. Parallel processing and sequencing allow a single technician to assay hundreds of samples per week at a reagent cost of around $10 USD per sample.
analysis.main_results: Across eight common hrHPV types (HPV16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 45, 52, and 58), HPV PhAM-Seq demonstrated >80% overall agreement with qPCR using degenerate L1-targeting primers, with the highest sensitivity for HPV16, 31, 33, and 58.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the method provides a scalable and cost-effective alternative to conventional qPCR for hrHPV genotyping, with improved sensitivity for certain types when using type-specific primers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV PhAM-Seq could be used for population-level surveillance and improve the efficiency of cervical cancer screening and vaccination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a blinded cohort of 170 cervical samples, and the evidence is based on a single methodological approach, which may affect generalisability and scalability.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces HPV Phased Amplicon Multiplex Sequencing (PhAM-Seq) as a cost-effective and scalable method for detecting high-risk human papillomaviruses (hrHPV) in cervical samples. The method uses combinatorial barcoding to enable higher throughput and lower per-sample costs compared to conventional sequencing approaches. Evaluated against the Seegene Anyplex II HPV28 Detection qPCR assay on a blinded cohort of 170 cervical samples, PhAM-Seq showed >80% overall agreement with qPCR using degenerate L1-targeting primers, with the highest sensitivity for HPV16, 31, 33, and 58. Sensitivity for HPV35, 45, and 52 improved to 85% or greater with type-specific primers targeting the E6/E7 gene loci. The authors interpret that PhAM-Seq offers a promising alternative for population-level surveillance and could enhance cervical cancer screening and vaccination strategies. However, the study is limited to a single methodological approach and a blinded cohort, which may affect its generalisability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发和评估一种经济有效的方法来检测高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV),以改进 宫颈癌 筛查和 疫苗接种 策略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用盲法 队列研究 评估了 HPV 定相扩增子多重测序 (PhAM-Seq),该样本包含 170 个宫颈样本,这些样本之前由 Seegene Anyplex II HPV28 检测 qPCR 分析进行分型。
elements_zh.methods: 该方法称为 HPV 定相扩增子多重测序 (PhAM-Seq),使用具有短、可变长度内联序列的扩增子组合条形码,与传统的扩增子测序方法相比,可实现更高的通量和更低的每个样本成本。并行处理和测序允许一名技术人员每周分析数百个样本,每个样本的试剂成本约为 10 美元。
elements_zh.main_results: 在八种常见的 hrHPV 类型(HPV16、18、31、33、35、45、52 和 58)中,HPV PhAM-Seq 与使用简并 L1 靶向引物的 qPCR 的总体一致性超过 80%,其中对 HPV16、31、33 和 58 的灵敏度最高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,该方法为 hrHPV 基因分型提供了一种可扩展且经济高效的替代传统 qPCR 的方法,并且在使用类型特异性引物时对某些类型的灵敏度有所提高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,HPV PhAM-Seq 可用于人群水平的 监测,并提高 宫颈癌 筛查和 疫苗接种 策略的效率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于 170 个宫颈样本的盲法 队列研究,并且证据基于单一方法,这可能会影响普遍性和可扩展性。

papers.title: Cervical Cancer Screening With Human Papillomavirus Self-Collection Testing in an Opioid Treatment Program
papers.abstract: Importance: Individuals with opioid use disorder and substance use disorder have lower cervical cancer screening rates than the general population. Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-collection testing provides opportunities to expand screening access to previously unreached patient populations. Objectives: To assess the feasibility and uptake of incorporating HPV self-collection testing for cervical cancer screening into routine care for patients with opioid use disorder and substance use disorder, and to track the rates of high-risk HPV and guideline concordant follow-up care in this population. Design, Setting, and Participants: This prospective cohort study was conducted from June 24, 2024, through December 31, 2025, at We Care Daily Clinics, a federally certified opioid treatment program (OTP) and American Indian Health Facility in Auburn, Washington. Eligible patients were 25 years or older, had a cervix, and were either overdue for cervical cancer screening or unsure of their last screening. Intervention: Screening using self-collection kits was offered during the patient's annual wellness visit, and self-collection occurred privately in the clinic restroom. Samples were analyzed for 14 high-risk HPV types at a laboratory. Screened patients with HPV-positive results received education and recommendations for guideline-concordant care. OTP staff facilitated patient referrals to local clinicians for gynecologic services, and follow-up was tracked. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcomes were the rates of HPV self-collection testing uptake, HPV positivity, and successful linkage to follow-up care. Results: A total of 194 patients (median [range] age, 41 [25-65] years) were evaluated. Of 174 patients (89.7%) eligible for cervical cancer screening, 158 (90.8%) completed HPV self-collection testing. There were 0 unsatisfactory test results, and 128 patients (81.0%) had HPV-negative results, 7 (4.4%) had HPV-16- or HPV-18-positive results, and 23 (14.6%) had positive results for other high-risk HPV types (non-HPV-16 or HPV-18 types only). Of the 30 patients with HPV-positive test results, 2 (6.7%) were lost to follow-up and 12 (40.0%) completed follow-up to date, which often required multiple coordination attempts by clinicians. The remaining 16 of 30 patients (53.3%) are currently actively engaged in various stages of referral and scheduling. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cohort study, incorporation of cervical cancer screening into an OTP using HPV self-collection testing was feasible with high patient eligibility and uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study evaluated the feasibility of HPV self-collection testing for cervical cancer screening in an opioid treatment program. Conducted at We Care Daily Clinics in Auburn, Washington, from June 2024 to December 2025, the study included 194 patients aged 25 or older with a cervix who were overdue or unsure of their last screening. Of 174 eligible patients, 158 (90.8%) completed self-collection testing, with 0 unsatisfactory results. Results showed 81.0% HPV-negative, 4.4% HPV-16/18-positive, and 14.6% positive for other high-risk HPV types. Among 30 HPV-positive patients, 12 (40.0%) completed follow-up, 16 (53.3%) were actively engaged in referral, and 2 (6.7%) were lost to follow-up. The study demonstrates high feasibility and uptake of self-collection testing in this underserved population, offering a promising approach to improve cervical cancer screening rates.

papers.title_zh: 在阿片类药物 治疗 计划中使用 人乳头瘤病毒 自收集测试进行 宫颈癌 筛查
papers.source_body_en: Importance: Individuals with opioid use disorder and substance use disorder have lower cervical cancer screening rates than the general population. Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-collection testing provides opportunities to expand screening access to previously unreached patient populations. Objectives: To assess the feasibility and uptake of incorporating HPV self-collection testing for cervical cancer screening into routine care for patients with opioid use disorder and substance use disorder, and to track the rates of high-risk HPV and guideline concordant follow-up care in this population. Design, Setting, and Participants: This prospective cohort study was conducted from June 24, 2024, through December 31, 2025, at We Care Daily Clinics, a federally certified opioid treatment program (OTP) and American Indian Health Facility in Auburn, Washington. Eligible patients were 25 years or older, had a cervix, and were either overdue for cervical cancer screening or unsure of their last screening. Intervention: Screening using self-collection kits was offered during the patient's annual wellness visit, and self-collection occurred privately in the clinic restroom. Samples were analyzed for 14 high-risk HPV types at a laboratory. Screened patients with HPV-positive results received education and recommendations for guideline-concordant care. OTP staff facilitated patient referrals to local clinicians for gynecologic services, and follow-up was tracked. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcomes were the rates of HPV self-collection testing uptake, HPV positivity, and successful linkage to follow-up care. Results: A total of 194 patients (median [range] age, 41 [25-65] years) were evaluated. Of 174 patients (89.7%) eligible for cervical cancer screening, 158 (90.8%) completed HPV self-collection testing. There were 0 unsatisfactory test results, and 128 patients (81.0%) had HPV-negative results, 7 (4.4%) had HPV-16- or HPV-18-positive results, and 23 (14.6%) had positive results for other high-risk HPV types (non-HPV-16 or HPV-18 types only). Of the 30 patients with HPV-positive test results, 2 (6.7%) were lost to follow-up and 12 (40.0%) completed follow-up to date, which often required multiple coordination attempts by clinicians. The remaining 16 of 30 patients (53.3%) are currently actively engaged in various stages of referral and scheduling. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cohort study, incorporation of cervical cancer screening into an OTP using HPV self-collection testing was feasible with high patient eligibility and uptake.
papers.abstract_zh: 重要性:患有阿片类药物使用障碍和物质使用障碍的个体的 宫颈癌 筛查率低于一般人群。人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 自采集检测提供了将筛查范围扩大到以前未覆盖的患者群体的机会。目的:评估将用于 宫颈癌 筛查的 HPV 自采集检测纳入阿片类药物使用障碍和物质使用障碍患者常规护理的可行性和采用情况,并跟踪该人群的 高危型HPV 率和指南一致的后续护理。设计、设置和参与者:这项前瞻性 队列研究 研究于 2024 年 6 月 24 日至 2025 年 12 月 31 日在 We Care Daily Clinics、联邦认证的阿片类药物 治疗 计划 (OTP) 和位于华盛顿州奥本的美国印第安人健康设施进行。符合资格的患者年龄为 25 岁或以上,有子宫颈,且逾期进行 宫颈癌 筛查或不确定上次筛查。干预:在患者年度健康访问期间,使用自我收集套件进行筛查,并在诊所卫生间私下进行自我收集。在实验室对样品进行了 14 种 高危型HPV 类型的分析。筛查出 HPV 阳性结果的患者接受了教育并获得了符合指南的护理建议。OTP 工作人员协助患者转诊至当地临床医生以获得妇科服务,并跟踪随访情况。主要结果和措施:主要结果是 HPV 自我采集检测的采用率、HPV 阳性率以及与后续护理的成功联系。结果:共有 194 名患者(中位年龄 [范围],41 [25-65] 岁)接受了评估。在 174 名符合 宫颈癌 筛查资格的患者 (89.7%) 中,158 名 (90.8%) 完成了 HPV 自我采集检测。0 例检测结果不理想,128 例患者 (81.0%) HPV 阴性结果,7 例 (4.4%) HPV-16 或 HPV-18 阳性结果,23 例 (14.6%) 其他 高危型HPV 型(仅限非 HPV-16 或 HPV-18 型)结果阳性。在 30 例 HPV 检测结果呈阳性的患者中,有 2 例 (6.7%) 失访,12 例 (40.0%) 迄今为止已完成随访,这通常需要临床医生进行多次协调尝试。30 名患者中的其余 16 名患者 (53.3%) 目前正在积极参与各个阶段的转诊和安排。结论和相关性:在这项 队列研究 研究中,将 宫颈癌 筛查纳入使用 HPV 自我收集检测的 OTP 中是可行的,患者资格和接受率很高。

papers.title: HPV16 E7-Associated SERPINB3 Suppression and MYC-Related Epithelial Plasticity in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection defines a distinct subtype of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Although HPV-positive (HPV+) HNSCC generally shows better overall survival than HPV-negative (HPV−) disease, it is frequently associated with cervical lymph node metastasis. However, the epithelial cell states and viral gene-associated mechanisms underlying HPV−related metastatic progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify metastasis-associated epithelial subpopulations in HPV+ HNSCC and explore the potential role of HPV16 E7 in regulating metastatic programs. Methods: Public single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from paired primary and metastatic HNSCC samples were integrated and analyzed to characterize malignant epithelial subpopulations. Copy number variation (CNV) inference, clustering, pathway enrichment, stemness scoring, and trajectory analysis were performed to define metastasis-associated epithelial states. TCGA transcriptomic data and tissue-based validation were used to support candidate gene screening. In vitro functional assays were performed using SERPINB3-knockdown and HPV16 early gene-overexpressing CAL27 cell models. Results: Single-cell analysis identified stem-like metastatic epithelial subpopulations in HPV+ and HPV− HNSCC. In HPV+ metastatic lesions, an ALDH2+/LAMB3+ epithelial subpopulation showed elevated epithelial–mesenchymal transition activity and stem-like features. SERPINB3 displayed a dynamic expression pattern during HPV+ metastatic progression. Functional assays showed that SERPINB3 knockdown enhanced CAL27 cell migration and invasion and was associated with activation of MYC- and epithelial–mesenchymal transition-related transcriptional programs. Among HPV16 early genes, E5, E6, E6*, and E7 showed different degrees of SERPINB3 suppression, while E7-expressing cells exhibited distinct transcriptional alterations associated with epithelial plasticity and metastatic-related programs. Conclusions: This study identifies a stem-like metastatic epithelial state in HPV-associated HNSCC and suggests a potential HPV16 early gene-SERPINB3-MYC-related regulatory mechanism involved in metastatic epithelial plasticity.

source_records.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection defines a distinct subtype of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). In vitro functional assays were performed using SERPINB3-knockdown and HPV16 early gene-overexpressing CAL27 cell models. Conclusions: This study identifies a stem-like metastatic epithelial state in HPV-associated HNSCC and suggests a potential HPV16 early gene-SERPINB3-MYC-related regulatory mechanism involved in metastatic epithelial plasticity.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates HPV-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), focusing on metastasis mechanisms. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染定义了头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 的一种独特亚型,尽管 HPV 阳性 (HPV+) HNSCC 通常比 HPV 阴性 (HPV−) 疾病表现出更好的总体生存率,但它经常与颈部淋巴结转移相关。

elements_zh.main_results: 单细胞分析确定了 HPV+ 和 HPV− HNSCC 中的干细胞样转移上皮亚群,其中 HPV+ 转移性病变中的 ALDH2+/LAMB3+ 上皮亚群显示出上皮-间质转化活性升高和干细胞样特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究鉴定了 HPV 相关 HNSCC 中的干细胞样转移上皮状态,并提出了与转移上皮可塑性相关的潜在 HPV16 早期基因 SERPINB3-MYC 相关调节机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为 HPV 相关转移进展的分子机制提供了见解,这可能为 HPV+ HNSCC 靶向治疗的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于公共数据集和体外模型,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性;然而,多种分析方法的整合支持中等水平的证据强度。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染定义了头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 的一种独特亚型。尽管 HPV 阳性 (HPV+) HNSCC 通常比 HPV 阴性 (HPV−) 疾病表现出更好的总体生存率,但它经常与颈部淋巴结转移相关。然而,HPV 相关转移进展的上皮细胞状态和病毒基因相关机制仍不完全清楚。本研究旨在鉴定 HPV+ HNSCC 中与转移相关的上皮亚群,并探讨 HPV16 E7 在调节转移程序中的潜在作用。方法:对来自配对的原发性和转移性 HNSCC 样本的公共单细胞 RNA 测序数据集进行整合和分析,以表征恶性上皮亚群。进行拷贝数变异(CNV)推断、聚类、通路富集、干性评分和轨迹分析来定义转移相关的上皮状态。TCGA 转录组数据和基于组织的验证用于支持候选基因筛选。使用 SERPINB3 敲低和 HPV16 早期基因过表达 CAL27 细胞模型进行体外功能测定。结果:单细胞分析鉴定出 HPV+ 和 HPV− HNSCC 中的干细胞样转移上皮亚群。在 HPV+ 转移性病变中,ALDH2+/LAMB3+ 上皮亚群表现出上皮-间质转化活性升高和干细胞样特征。SERPINB3 在 HPV+ 转移进展过程中表现出动态表达模式。功能分析表明,SERPINB3 敲除增强了 CAL27 细胞迁移和侵袭,并与 MYC 和上皮间质转化相关转录程序的激活相关。在HPV16早期基因中,E5、E6、E6*和E7表现出不同程度的SERPINB3抑制,而表达E7的细胞表现出与上皮可塑性和转移相关程序相关的明显转录改变。结论:本研究鉴定了 HPV 相关 HNSCC 中的干细胞样转移上皮状态,并提出了参与转移上皮可塑性的潜在 HPV16 早期基因 -SERPINB3-MYC 相关调节机制。

papers.title: Three-year persistence and clearance patterns of high-risk HPV genotype groups among women in Chirchik, Uzbekistan: A pilot longitudinal study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) persistence is central to cervical carcinogenesis, yet longitudinal data from Central Asia remain limited. This pilot longitudinal study assessed the distribution of hrHPV genotype groups and 3-year follow-up patterns among women in Chirchik, Uzbekistan. Methods From August 2021 to March 2022, 5,678 women were screened for hrHPV, of whom 547 (9.6%) tested positive. HPV genotyping was performed using the Xpert HPV assay. Single infections were defined as the detection of one genotype group, while multiple infections were defined as the detection of two or more groups. Clearance was defined as a negative HPV test at 3-year follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox regression were used for analysis. Results Single infections predominated at baseline (87.0%, 476/547), while double, triple, and quadruple infections accounted for 11.2%, 1.5%, and 0.2% of cases, respectively. The most frequently detected genotype groups were HPV16 (29.8%), HPV31/33/35/52/58 (19.9%), and HPV39/56/66/68 (16.5%). At 3-year follow-up, 409 baseline hrHPV-positive women were re-evaluated, and 108 remained hrHPV-positive. Single infections remained predominant among persistent hrHPV-positive cases (94.4%, 102/108). HPV16 was the most frequently detected genotype group at follow-up (38.0%), followed by HPV39/56/66/68 (24.1%) and HPV31/33/35/52/58 (19.4%). Newly detected genotype groups were observed in 36 women, with HPV39/56/66/68 being the most common (52.8%). Clearance rates were numerically higher in selected HPV16 -containing co-infection groups than in single HPV16 infection, but no statistically significant difference was observed (log-rank p = 0.528). Conclusion This pilot study provides preliminary longitudinal evidence on the distribution of hrHPV genotype groups and 3-year follow-up patterns in Uzbekistan. Larger studies with repeated follow-up testing and genotype-level analysis are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Evaluation and comparison of large language model responses to patient questions after diagnosis of high-risk human papillomavirus infection: an expert-rated digital patient education study
papers.abstract: Background After diagnosis of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, patients often seek guidance on cancer risk, colposcopy, follow-up, treatment, partner management, pregnancy, and anxiety. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical consultation, but their response quality and safety in this setting require evaluation. Methods In this single-center, expert-rated methodological study, 15 patient-style questions based on common outpatient consultations were submitted to ChatGPT-5.5 Instant and DeepSeek-V3. Each model generated three independent responses per question, yielding 90 artificial intelligence (AI)-generated responses. Five blinded gynecology experts independently evaluated all responses, producing 450 expert-rating records. Accuracy, safety, guideline concordance, completeness, and understandability were rated on a 1–5 Likert scale. Experts also assessed major error and potential harm. The primary outcome was the proportion of responses without major error or potential harm. Results ChatGPT-5.5 Instant had higher response-level scores than DeepSeek-V3 for accuracy (mean difference, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.11–0.39; FDR-adjusted p = 0.010), safety (0.27; 0.07–0.47; p = 0.010), completeness (0.22; 0.07–0.37; p = 0.020), and composite score (0.18; 0.04–0.31; p = 0.027). The difference in guideline concordance did not remain significant after multiplicity correction (0.16; −0.01 to 0.33; FDR-adjusted p = 0.057), and understandability was similar. Responses without major error or potential harm occurred in 42/45 (93.3%; 95% CI, 81.7–98.6%) ChatGPT responses and 38/45 (84.4%; 70.5–93.5%) DeepSeek-V3 responses (risk difference, 8.9 percentage points; 95% CI, −13.3 to 31.1; p = 0.344). Exploratory question-level risks were observed in HPV16/18 positivity, normal cytology, partner management, and pregnancy scenarios. Conclusion Both two models demonstrated generally strong performance across the evaluated quality domains. ChatGPT achieved higher ratings in several quality domains, but response-level binary safety differences were imprecise and not statistically significant. Both models require guideline-based clinical oversight.

Responses without major error or potential harm occurred in 42/45 (93.3%; 95% CI, 81.7–98.6%) ChatGPT responses and 38/45 (84.4%; 70.5–93.5%) DeepSeek-V3 responses (risk difference, 8.9 percentage points; 95% CI, −13.3 to 31.1; p = 0.344). Exploratory question-level risks were observed in HPV16/18 positivity, normal cytology, partner management, and pregnancy scenarios. Conclusion Both two models demonstrated generally strong performance across the evaluated quality domains. ChatGPT achieved higher ratings in several quality domains, but response-level binary safety differences were imprecise and not statistically significant. Both models require guideline-based clinical oversight.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 在感染高危 诊断 (HPV) 后,患者经常寻求有关癌症风险、随访、治疗、伴侣管理、怀孕和焦虑的指导,这凸显了对可靠的数字患者教育资源的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项单中心、专家评级的方法学研究向两个大型语言模型 (LLM) 提交了 15 个患者风格的问题,生成了 90 个人工智能生成的答案,并由五位盲法妇科专家进行评估,产生了 450 条专家评级记录。
analysis_zh.methods: 基于常见门诊咨询的 15 个患者风格的问题被提交给 ChatGPT-5.5 Instant 和 DeepSeek-V3,每个问题生成三个独立的答复。五位盲法妇科专家使用 1-5 李克特量表独立评估了所有回答的准确性、安全性、指南一致性、完整性和可理解性,并评估了重大错误和潜在危害。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种模型在评估的质量领域中都表现出了强劲的性能,ChatGPT 在多个领域获得了更高的评级,尽管二元安全性差异不精确且不具有统计显着性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,法学硕士可以对患者有关 高危型HPV 感染的问题提供高质量、符合指南的答复,但这两种模型都需要临床监督以减轻潜在风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到单中心设计的限制,依赖专家评级而不是患者结果,并且缺乏评估模型和问题之外的普遍性,需要进行适度的置信度评估。

papers.full_text: 134 Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV-16, is now a leading cause of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), transmitted primarily through oral exposure. Despite rising incidence, clinical awareness of its variable presentations remains limited. Early recognition is essential because airway compromise may progress rapidly even when initial imaging appears benign. CASE DESCRIPTION A 37-year-old woman experienced 14 months of progressive cervical lymphadenopathy, dysphagia, dysphonia, and ultimately right brachial plexopathy. She underwent eight hospitalizations without lymph node biopsy and received multiple rounds of steroids and/or antibiotics, which temporarily masked progression. She later developed stridor and presented to the emergency department where computed tomography was interpreted as negative and she was discharged. Persistent clinical concern prompted direct physician–radiologist communication and independent reinterpretation of imaging, which revealed extensive cervical lymphadenopathy with near-complete nasopharyngeal obstruction and marked lingual tonsillar enlargement compressing the soft palate. The patient returned emergently with impending airway compromise. Severe upper-airway obstruction secondary to HPV-16–positive, p16-positive OPSCC with bulky nodal disease and neurologic involvement. The patient required emergent intubation for impending airway compromise using a pediatric-sized endotracheal tube, followed by tracheotomy and four days of mechanical ventilation before definitive biopsy and diagnosis. Coordinated airway management and expedited oncologic evaluation were essential for stabilization. Histopathology confirmed HPV-16–positive squamous cell carcinoma involving the naso- and oropharynx. The patient gradually weaned from ventilatory support and recovered after approximately 11–12 days of airway stabilization. She was discharged to rehabilitation to improve functional status while awaiting PET-CT staging and initiation of definitive chemoradiation therapy. Discussion This case illustrates how a siloed clinical approach, delayed biopsy, and reliance on transient steroid response can obscure a rapidly evolving malignancy. Cross-disciplinary review of patient presentations helps identify alternative pathologies and prompts earlier consideration of alternative diagnoses and management strategies. This is imperative when presentations mimic benign infection such as HPV-16. A structured approach including early consideration of HPV-related etiologies, prompt tissue diagnosis in persistent or progressive lymphadenopathy, and coordinated multidisciplinary communication may reduce diagnostic delay and prevent life-threatening airway emergencies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the limited clinical awareness of variable presentations of HPV-16–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), emphasizing the need for early recognition to prevent rapid airway compromise.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 37-year-old woman with progressive cervical lymphadenopathy, dysphagia, dysphonia, and right brachial plexopathy who experienced multiple hospitalizations before definitive diagnosis.
analysis.methods: The patient underwent emergent intubation, tracheotomy, mechanical ventilation, and definitive biopsy to confirm HPV-16–positive squamous cell carcinoma involving the naso- and oropharynx.
analysis.main_results: Imaging revealed extensive cervical lymphadenopathy with near-complete nasopharyngeal obstruction and marked lingual tonsillar compression; histopathology confirmed HPV-16–positive OPSCC with bulky nodal disease and neurologic involvement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that siloed clinical approaches, delayed biopsy, and transient steroid responses can obscure rapidly evolving malignancies, highlighting the need for cross-disciplinary review to identify alternative pathologies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A structured approach including early consideration of HPV-related etiologies, prompt tissue diagnosis in persistent lymphadenopathy, and multidisciplinary communication may reduce diagnostic delays and prevent life-threatening airway emergencies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the case report design, which lacks generalizability, but the detailed clinical course and histopathological confirmation provide moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This case report highlights a 37-year-old woman with HPV-16–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma presenting as regional head-and-neck lymphadenopathy with dysphagia and dysphonia, leading to life-threatening airway compromise. Despite multiple hospitalizations and imaging initially interpreted as negative, cross-disciplinary review revealed extensive disease requiring emergent airway management. The study underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis and multidisciplinary coordination to prevent diagnostic delays in HPV-associated malignancies with atypical presentations.

elements_en.main_results: Imaging revealed extensive cervical lymphadenopathy with near-complete nasopharyngeal obstruction and marked lingual tonsillar compression; histopathology confirmed HPV-16–positive OPSCC with bulky nodal disease and neurologic involvement.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that siloed clinical approaches, delayed biopsy, and transient steroid responses can obscure rapidly evolving malignancies, highlighting the need for cross-disciplinary review to identify alternative pathologies.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A structured approach including early consideration of HPV-related etiologies, prompt tissue diagnosis in persistent lymphadenopathy, and multidisciplinary communication may reduce diagnostic delays and prevent life-threatening airway emergencies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the case report design, which lacks generalizability, but the detailed clinical course and histopathological confirmation provide moderate confidence in the findings.

papers.title: Comparison of cervical swab and urine samples for high-risk HPV infection and PAX1 methylation in detection of cervical neoplasia
papers.abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer screening commonly requires clinician-collected cervical specimens, prompting interest in less invasive sampling approaches. This paired pilot study assessed agreement in high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) detection and PAX1 methylation testing between cervical swab and urine specimens and evaluated their performance for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3+). We enrolled 104 women with abnormal cervical cytology and histopathological confirmation. Among 94 pairs with valid hrHPV results, overall agreement was 94.7% (Cohen’s κ = 0.883; 95% CI, 0.783–0.983). Among 91 pairs with valid PAX1 results, agreement was 79.1% (κ = 0.446; 95% CI, 0.241–0.651). For CIN3 + detection, cervical swab and urine hrHPV testing showed sensitivities of 86.8% and 80.6% and specificities of 44.4% and 45.9%, respectively. Cervical swab and urine PAX1 methylation showed lower sensitivities of 52.6% and 41.2% but higher specificities of 85.7% and 90.0%, respectively. Rule-based combinations showed sensitivity–specificity trade-offs. In this referral-based cohort, urine hrHPV testing showed high agreement with cervical swab testing, whereas urine PAX1 methylation had lower agreement and sensitivity. Urine-based PAX1 testing remains exploratory and requires optimization and independent validation.

papers.title_zh: 宫颈拭子和尿液样本 高危型HPV 感染和 PAX1 甲基化检测宫颈肿瘤的比较
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Cervical cancer screening commonly requires clinician-collected cervical specimens, prompting interest in less invasive sampling approaches. This paired pilot study assessed agreement in high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) detection and PAX1 methylation testing between cervical swab and urine specimens and evaluated their performance for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse (CIN3+). We enrolled 104 women with abnormal cervical cytology and histopathological confirmation. Among 94 pairs with valid hrHPV results, overall agreement was 94.7% (Cohen’s κ = 0.883; 95% CI, 0.783–0.983). Among 91 pairs with valid PAX1 results, agreement was 79.1% (κ = 0.446; 95% CI, 0.241–0.651). For CIN3 + detection, cervical swab and urine hrHPV testing showed sensitivities of 86.8% and 80.6% and specificities of 44.4% and 45.9%, respectively. Cervical swab and urine PAX1 methylation showed lower sensitivities of 52.6% and 41.2% but higher specificities of 85.7% and 90.0%, respectively. Rule-based combinations showed sensitivity–specificity trade-offs. In this referral-based cohort, urine hrHPV testing showed high agreement with cervical swab testing, whereas urine PAX1 methylation had lower agreement and sensitivity. Urine-based PAX1 testing remains exploratory and requires optimization and independent validation.

papers.title: Efficacy of live lactobacillus preparations in treating cervical inflammation and clearing viral infections in patients with HPV infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Dingjunsheng, a live Lactobacillus preparation, as adjuvant therapy in patients with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection complicated by bacterial vaginosis (BV). A retrospective analysis was conducted on 152 eligible patients, randomly divided into two groups: the observation group (n=87) receiving standard BV antibacterial therapy plus Dingjunsheng, and the control group (n=65) who received standard BV antibacterial therapy alone. The patients were followed up for six months. Primary outcomes included HPV clearance rate and cervical cytological inflammation improvement, while secondary outcomes involved BV recurrence rate and adverse reaction incidence. The results showed that the observation group had a significantly higher HPV clearance rate (73.6% vs 53.9%) and inflammation improvement rate (90.8% vs 76.9%), as well as a lower BV recurrence rate (3.1% vs 13.9%) compared to the control group. Dingjunsheng was identified as an independent protective factor for HPV clearance (OR=2.5, 95%CI:1.3–5.1). The incidence of adverse reactions was similar between both groups. We conclude that Dingjunsheng adjuvant therapy demonstrated effectiveness in improving HPV clearance, alleviating inflammation, and reducing BV recurrence, with good safety, making it a valuable treatment strategy for these patients.

papers.title: HPV vaccination in the WHO South-East Asia Region: A scoping review of uptake, implementation challenges, and pathways to acceleration.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health concern in the WHO South-East Asia Region (SEAR), where human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage remains uneven. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on HPV vaccine uptake and implementation strategies and challenges across SEAR countries. Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-Scoping Review (ScR) guidelines, 46 studies published between January 2003 and February 2026 were analyzed. Ten of eleven SEAR countries have introduced HPV vaccination nationally, with Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and Thailand achieving coverage above 90%, while several countries remain in early implementation or expansion phases. Four cross-cutting barriers were identified: policy and financial constraints, sociocultural resistance, weak health-system capacity, and vaccine hesitancy. Based on these findings, SEAR-HPV Integrated Implementation Model (SHIM) is proposed to strengthen policy support, sustainable financing, community engagement, workforce preparedness, and digital monitoring. This review highlights evidence-informed strategies to accelerate HPV vaccine scale-up and advance cervical cancer elimination goals in the region.

papers.source_body_en: Cervical cancer remains a major public health concern in the WHO South-East Asia Region (SEAR), where human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage remains uneven. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on HPV vaccine uptake and implementation strategies and challenges across SEAR countries. Following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-Scoping Review (ScR) guidelines, 46 studies published between January 2003 and February 2026 were analyzed. Ten of eleven SEAR countries have introduced HPV vaccination nationally, with Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and Thailand achieving coverage above 90%, while several countries remain in early implementation or expansion phases. Four cross-cutting barriers were identified: policy and financial constraints, sociocultural resistance, weak health-system capacity, and vaccine hesitancy. Based on these findings, SEAR-HPV Integrated Implementation Model (SHIM) is proposed to strengthen policy support, sustainable financing, community engagement, workforce preparedness, and digital monitoring. This review highlights evidence-informed strategies to accelerate HPV vaccine scale-up and advance cervical cancer elimination goals in the region.

papers.title: Effect of Self-Sampling HPV DNA Testing on Cervical Cancer Screening in Singapore's Primary Care: Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Singapore, cervical cancer screening rates remain suboptimal, with only clinician sampling included in the national screening program. Self-sampling human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing might overcome barriers to clinician-based screening and improve uptake. We assessed the effect of offering self-sampling alongside clinician sampling on screening uptake and high-risk HPV detection compared with clinician sampling alone. METHODS: This pragmatic, 2-arm randomized controlled trial with Zelen design was conducted across NHG Polyclinics, NHG Health in Singapore. Women aged 30-69 years due for cervical cancer screening were randomly assigned (1:1) to intervention (offered selection of clinician sampling followed by self-sampling) or usual care (clinician sampling alone). The primary outcome was high-risk HPV DNA detection, and the secondary outcome was screening uptake. We performed subgroup analysis to examine both outcomes by prior screening history. Multivariable analysis identified factors associated with screening choices. RESULTS: From August 2024 to February 2025, 650 women were randomized, and 640 were included in the analysis (320 per arm). Significantly more high-risk HPV was detected in the intervention arm (3.1% vs 0.3%; absolute difference 2.8%; 95% CI, 0.8-4.8;P < .001), driven by greater screening uptake (56.6% vs 42.8%; absolute difference 13.8%; 95% CI, 6.0-21.4; P < .001), particularly among women with regular screening history and those with no prior screening. Among screened participants in the intervention arm, 56.4% chose self-sampling. Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of choosing self-sampling over declining screening. CONCLUSIONS: Offering self-sampling HPV DNA testing alongside clinician sampling significantly increased screening uptake and high-risk HPV detection rates. However, uptake remained lower among women with less education, highlighting the need for targeted engagement strategies.Abstract also available in: عربي (Arabic); Deutsch (German); Español (Spanish); Francais (French); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesia (Indonesian); (Chinese); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese).

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在新加坡,宫颈癌 筛查率仍然不理想,国家筛查计划中仅包括临床医生抽样。自采样 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) DNA 检测可能会克服基于临床医生的筛查的障碍并提高采用率。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项采用 Zelen 设计的务实 2 组随机对照试验在新加坡 NHG 综合诊所和 NHG Health 进行。需要进行 宫颈癌 筛查的 30-69 岁女性被随机分配 (1:1) 进行干预(提供临床医生抽样选择,然后自行抽样)或常规护理(仅临床医生抽样)。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果是 高危型HPV DNA 检测,次要结果是筛选摄取。我们进行了亚组分析,通过先前的筛查历史检查这两种结果,并进行多变量分析,以确定与筛查选择相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: From August 2024 to February 2025, 650 women were randomized, and 640 were included in the analysis (320 per arm). Significantly more high-risk HPV was detected in the intervention arm (3.1% vs 0.3%; absolute difference 2.8%; 95% CI, 0.8-4.8; P < .001), driven by greater screening uptake (56.6% vs 42.8%; absolute difference 13.8%; 95% CI, 6.0-21.4; P < .001), particularly among women with regular screening history and those with no prior screening.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 提供自我采样 HPV DNA 检测和临床医生采样显着提高了筛查率和 高危型HPV 检出率。然而,受教育程度较低的女性的参与度仍然较低,这凸显了制定有针对性的参与战略的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,自我采样 HPV DNA 检测可以提高初级保健机构中 宫颈癌 筛查覆盖率和 高危型HPV 感染的早期发现。这种方法对于接受临床医生筛查的机会有限的女性特别有益。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在单一医疗保健系统中进行的,这可能会限制对其他环境的推广。尽管采用了随机设计,但由于试验的务实性质以及自我抽样选择中可能存在选择偏差,证据强度中等。

Significantly more high-risk HPV was detected in the intervention arm (3.1% vs 0.3%; absolute difference 2.8%; 95% CI, 0.8-4.8;P < .001), driven by greater screening uptake (56.6% vs 42.8%; absolute difference 13.8%; 95% CI, 6.0-21.4; P < .001), particularly among women with regular screening history and those with no prior screening. Among screened participants in the intervention arm, 56.4% chose self-sampling. Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of choosing self-sampling over declining screening. CONCLUSIONS: Offering self-sampling HPV DNA testing alongside clinician sampling significantly increased screening uptake and high-risk HPV detection rates. However, uptake remained lower among women with less education, highlighting the need for targeted engagement strategies.Abstract also available in: عربي (Arabic); Deutsch (German); Español (Spanish); Francais (French); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesia (Indonesian); (Chinese); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese).

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 在新加坡,宫颈癌 筛查率仍然不理想,国家筛查计划中仅包括临床医生抽样。自采样 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) DNA 检测可能会克服基于临床医生的筛查的障碍并提高采用率。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项采用 Zelen 设计的务实 2 组随机对照试验在新加坡 NHG 综合诊所和 NHG Health 进行。需要进行 宫颈癌 筛查的 30-69 岁女性被随机分配 (1:1) 进行干预(提供临床医生抽样选择,然后自行抽样)或常规护理(仅临床医生抽样)。
analysis_zh.methods: 主要结果是 高危型HPV DNA 检测,次要结果是筛选摄取。我们进行了亚组分析,通过先前的筛查历史检查这两种结果,并进行多变量分析,以确定与筛查选择相关的因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 提供自我采样 HPV DNA 检测和临床医生采样显着提高了筛查率和 高危型HPV 检出率。然而,受教育程度较低的女性的参与度仍然较低,这凸显了制定有针对性的参与战略的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,自我采样 HPV DNA 检测可以提高初级保健机构中 宫颈癌 筛查覆盖率和 高危型HPV 感染的早期发现。这种方法对于接受临床医生筛查的机会有限的女性特别有益。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在单一医疗保健系统中进行的,这可能会限制对其他环境的推广。尽管采用了随机设计,但由于试验的务实性质以及自我抽样选择中可能存在选择偏差,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Esophageal Squamous Papilloma in the Practice of Otolaryngology: A Case Series and Diagnostic Considerations for the otolaryngologist.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous papilloma (ESP) is a rare, benign, often asymptomatic lesion of the upper aerodigestive tract. While historically managed by gastroenterologists, transnasal esophagoscopy has been incorporated into some otolaryngology practices, expanding the role of the otolaryngologist in diagnosing these lesions. AIMS: To describe a case series of ESP within a tertiary dysphagia center and evaluate the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and chronic mucosal irritation. METHODS: A retrospective case series was conducted of all individuals diagnosed with ESP at a tertiary center over a 2-year period. Histopathology and DNA in-situ hybridization (ISH) for high and low-risk HPV were reviewed. RESULTS: Five cases were identified. All patients presented with dysphagia or heartburn. ESP was an incidental finding in all cases, co-existing with cricopharyngeal dysfunction, hiatal hernia, or esophagitis. One patient had a history of HPV+ oropharyngeal carcinoma. All lesions were successfully resected endoscopically. ISH was negative for HPV in all specimens. CONCLUSIONS AND SIGNIFICANCE: ESP is a benign entity frequently encountered incidentally during the workup of dysphagia. These results support chronic irritation rather than HPV as the primary etiology. Recognition is vital for otolaryngologists to ensure appropriate resection and surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:食管鳞状乳头状瘤(ESP)是一种罕见的良性上呼吸消化道病变,通常无症状。虽然历史上由胃肠病学家管理,但经鼻食管镜检查已被纳入一些耳鼻喉科实践中,扩大了耳鼻喉科医师在诊断这些病变中的作用。目的:描述三级吞咽困难中心内的 ESP 病例系列,并评估 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 与慢性粘膜刺激之间的关联。方法:对 2 年时间内在三级中心诊断为 ESP 的所有个体进行回顾性病例系列研究。对高危和低危 HPV 的组织病理学和 DNA 原位杂交 (ISH) 进行了综述。结果:发现 5 例病例。所有患者均出现吞咽困难或胃灼热。所有病例中 ESP 都是偶然发现的,与环咽功能障碍、食管裂孔疝或食管炎并存。一名患者有 HPV+ 口咽癌病史。所有病变均通过内镜成功切除。所有标本中 ISH 的 HPV 均为阴性。结论和意义:ESP 是一种良性实体,经常在吞咽困难检查过程中偶然遇到。这些结果支持慢性刺激而不是 HPV 为主要病因。认可对于耳鼻喉科医生确保适当的切除和 监测 至关重要。

papers.title: Circulating Tumor DNA in Head and Neck Cancer: A Review From the American Head and Neck Society.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Despite gains in understanding head and neck cancer over the past several decades, the discovery of reliable biomarkers remains elusive. With the advent of human papillomavirus-associated oropharynx cancer and Epstein-Barr virus-associated nasopharynx cancer, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and oncogenic viral DNA have emerged as potentially promising biomarkers. OBSERVATIONS: A review was conducted by the American Head and Neck Society to address the current utility of ctDNA. Ongoing clinical trials were reviewed, with discussion of its utility in monitoring treatment response and measuring minimal residual disease (MRD). Although ctDNA holds promise in the push for precision oncology, several questions remain regarding its routine clinical use, including test variability and implications of inaccurate test results. Optimized clinical trial designs and further research are necessary to bring ctDNA to the forefront of head and neck cancer management. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Liquid biopsy targeting viral ctDNA is a promising biomarker in the diagnostic and surveillance settings across head and neck cancer types. Ongoing clinical trials will help elucidate how ctDNA can be implemented to monitor treatment response, assess MRD, and frame treatment decisions to adapt treatment via a precision oncology approach.

papers.title: Female allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant survivors' perspectives on cervical cancer screening: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Female allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (AlloHCT) survivors are at increased risk for human papillomavirus (HPV)-related malignancies due to immunosuppression. Guidelines recommend annual cervical cancer screening for AlloHCT survivors with a cervix aged 21-65. This study explored cervical cancer screening knowledge, behaviors, attitudes, experiences, and preferences-specifically provider-collected versus self-collected methods-and identified adherence barriers and facilitators. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods observational study of female AlloHCT survivors aged 21-65 who received AlloHCT at Oregon Health & Science University between 2012 and 2023. Participants completed demographic surveys and participated in focus groups exploring screening adherence, perceptions, and preferences. RESULTS: Twenty-three survivors completed the survey, and 16 joined focus groups in fall 2024. The median participant age was 49 years (range 32-61); most were white (87%) and privately insured (91%). Median age at bone marrow transplantation (BMT) was 41 years (range 19-56). Primary diagnosis included acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome (65%). Reported complications included graft versus host disease (GVHD) (44%), chronic GVHD (39%), and vaginal GVHD (22%). Awareness of increased cervical cancer risk facilitated screening adherence, while limited access to in-network providers was a barrier. All participants preferred provider-collected screening due to confidence in test accuracy and reassurance from clinician involvement. Psychological factors, particularly worrying about recurrence or secondary cancers, strongly influenced screening preferences. CONCLUSION: Cervical cancer screening preferences among AlloHCT survivors were shaped by physical and psychological treatment-related factors. HPV self-collection may be a supplemental option before BMT, between annual clinic visits, or when access barriers arise.

Results Twenty-three survivors completed the survey, and 16 joined focus groups in fall 2024. The median participant age was 49 years (range 32-61); most were white (87%) and privately insured (91%). Reported complications included graft versus host disease (GVHD) (44%), chronic GVHD (39%), and vaginal GVHD (22%). All participants preferred provider-collected screening due to confidence in test accuracy and reassurance from clinician involvement. Psychological factors, particularly worrying about recurrence or secondary cancers, strongly influenced screening preferences. HPV self-collection may be a supplemental option before BMT, between annual clinic visits, or when access barriers arise.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A mixed-methods observational study was conducted with female AlloHCT survivors who received transplants at Oregon Health & Science University between 2012 and 2023. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Cervical cancer screening preferences among AlloHCT survivors are shaped by physical and psychological treatment-related factors. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study identified limited access to in-network providers as a barrier to screening adherence. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore strategies to improve access to in-network providers and address psychological barriers to screening. analysis.summary_en: This mixed-methods study examined cervical cancer screening perspectives among female AlloHCT survivors, who face elevated HPV-related malignancy risks due to immunosuppression. Participants preferred provider-collected screening for its accuracy and clinician reassurance, though psychological factors like cancer recurrence worries influenced decisions. Barriers included limited access to in-network providers, while awareness of increased risk facilitated adherence. The study suggests HPV self-collection could supplement annual screening, particularly before BMT or during access challenges. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions addressing both physical and psychological factors to improve screening adherence in this high-risk population.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究重点关注 21-65 岁的女性同种异体造血细胞移植 (AlloHCT) 幸存者,她们因免疫抑制而面临 HPV 相关恶性肿瘤的风险增加。中心问题探讨他们的 宫颈癌 筛选知识、行为、态度、经验和偏好,特别是比较提供者收集的方法与自我收集的方法,同时识别依从障碍和促进因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 对 2012 年至 2023 年间在俄勒冈健康与科学大学接受移植的女性 AlloHCT 幸存者进行了一项混合方法观察性研究。参与者完成了人口调查和焦点小组,以探索筛查依从性、看法和偏好。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: AlloHCT 幸存者的 宫颈癌 筛查偏好是由生理和心理 治疗 相关因素决定的。由于对测试准确性的信心以及临床医生参与的保证,所有参与者都更喜欢提供者收集的筛查。HPV 自我采集可以作为 BMT 之前、每年访视之间或出现获取障碍时的补充选择。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究发现,与网络内提供者的接触有限是筛选依从性的障碍。心理因素,特别是对复发或继发性癌症的担忧,强烈影响偏好,但该研究并未解决更广泛的系统或地理访问差异。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应探索改善网络内医疗服务提供者的接触机会并解决筛查心理障碍的策略。实践意义包括考虑将 HPV 自我采集作为克服获取障碍的补充选择,同时保持每年提供者采集的筛查作为首选方法。

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:由于免疫抑制,女性同种异体造血细胞移植 (AlloHCT) 幸存者患 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关恶性肿瘤的风险增加。指南建议每年对宫颈年龄为 21-65 岁的 AlloHCT 幸存者进行 宫颈癌 筛查。本研究探讨了 宫颈癌 筛查知识、行为、态度、经验和偏好(特别是提供者收集与自我收集的方法),并确定了依从性障碍和促进因素。方法:我们对 2012 年至 2023 年间在俄勒冈健康与科学大学接受 AlloHCT 的 21-65 岁女性 AlloHCT 幸存者进行了一项混合方法观察研究。参与者完成了人口统计调查,并参加了焦点小组,探讨筛查依从性、看法和偏好。结果:23 名幸存者完成了调查,16 名幸存者于 2024 年秋季加入了焦点小组。参与者年龄中位数为 49 岁(范围 32-61);大多数是白人(87%)和私人保险(91%)。骨髓移植 (BMT) 的中位年龄为 41 岁(范围 19-56 岁)。原发性 诊断 包括急性髓系白血病或骨髓增生异常综合征 (65%)。报告的并发症包括移植物抗 宿主 病 (GVHD) (44%)、慢性 GVHD (39%) 和阴道 GVHD (22%)。对 宫颈癌 风险增加的认识促进了筛查依从性,而对网络内提供者的访问有限是一个障碍。由于对测试准确性的信心以及临床医生参与的保证,所有参与者都更喜欢提供者收集的筛查。心理因素,特别是担心复发或继发性癌症,强烈影响筛查偏好。结论:AlloHCT 幸存者的 宫颈癌 筛查偏好是由生理和心理 治疗 相关因素决定的。自行收集 HPV 可能是 BMT 之前、年度门诊就诊之间或出现获取障碍时的补充选择。

papers.title: Squamous Cell Anal Carcinoma: Current Therapeutic Approaches.
papers.abstract: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (SCAC) is a relatively rare malignancy, but its incidence has been rising, largely due to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), which is the main etiological driver. HPV vaccination and treatment of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) significantly lower the risk of progression to invasive cancer, while immunosuppressed individuals face a higher susceptibility to disease development. Most patients are diagnosed with localized SCAC, for which definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy remains the standard of care, offering high rates of disease control and overall survival Metastatic disease carries a poor prognosis and is primarily managed with systemic therapy with platinum-based chemotherapy is the preferred first-line treatment; recent phase III data established the combination of carboplatin-paclitaxel with retifanlimab (anti-PD1) as a new standard. Ongoing research is focused on HPV-targeted strategies and novel immunotherapies, which hold promise for further improving outcomes in both early and advanced stages of SCAC.

Most patients are diagnosed with localized SCAC, for which definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy remains the standard of care, offering high rates of disease control and overall survival Metastatic disease carries a poor prognosis and is primarily managed with systemic therapy with platinum-based chemotherapy is the preferred first-line treatment; recent phase III data established the combination of carboplatin-paclitaxel with retifanlimab (anti-PD1) as a new standard. Ongoing research is focused on HPV-targeted strategies and novel immunotherapies, which hold promise for further improving outcomes in both early and advanced stages of SCAC.

papers.title: Implementation and impact of primary HPV testing in cervical cancer screening: Historical perspectives and institutional experience at a large academic medical center.
papers.abstract: Recognition of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) as the etiologic agent in nearly all cervical cancers has fundamentally reshaped screening strategies, driving the development and adoption of highly sensitive molecular HPV assays. Over the past several decades, cervical cancer screening guidelines have shifted from primarily cytology-based approaches toward HPV-based modalities, with primary HPV testing now recommended as the preferred method by the American Cancer Society and anticipated to be similarly endorsed by the United States Preventive Services Task Force. This article traces the evolution of cervical cancer screening, from the original Papanicolaou test to current guideline recommendations, and discusses the logistical requirements for transitioning to a primary HPV screening system, including triage strategies for HPV-positive cases. The authors additionally present an institutional experience of initiating primary HPV testing, highlighting its impact on cytopathology laboratory workflow and specimen volumes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomavirus (HPV) as the etiologic agent in cervical cancer and the evolution of screening strategies toward primary HPV testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a historical and institutional review tracing the evolution of cervical cancer screening from cytology-based approaches to HPV-based modalities, with no explicit systematic search or meta-analysis reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Primary HPV testing is now the preferred screening method per the American Cancer Society and anticipated endorsement by the USPSTF, with high sensitivity for detecting cervical cancer precursors.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights logistical challenges in transitioning to primary HPV testing, including triage strategies for HPV-positive cases, but does not address broader evidence gaps or conflicting findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The authors emphasize the need for institutional planning to manage workflow and specimen volume changes during the transition to primary HPV testing.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical shift from cytology-based to HPV-based cervical cancer screening, driven by the recognition of HPV as the primary etiologic agent. It details the evolution of guidelines, with primary HPV testing now preferred by the American Cancer Society and anticipated endorsement by the USPSTF. The authors present institutional experience, highlighting logistical requirements and workflow impacts during the transition, including triage strategies for HPV-positive cases. While consensus supports HPV testing's sensitivity, the review underscores practical implementation challenges without addressing broader evidence gaps.

papers.title: Differentiation-independent activation of HPV genome replication by the lncRNA DINO.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) rely on multiple host cell factors to replicate the viral genome, yet the contribution of host long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to viral genome maintenance and amplification in the productive life cycle remains poorly understood. In this study, we show that the lncRNA damage-induced long non-coding RNA (DINO) is a driver of HPV DNA replication. DINO levels increase during keratinocyte differentiation, and ectopic expression of DINO promotes both HPV genome replication and the formation of replication foci, and this is independent of keratinocyte differentiation signals. Ectopic DINO expression increases select early viral transcript levels, including E1^E4, E1, and E2. Notably, DINO’s subcellular localization is also context-dependent: during DNA damage, DINO is predominantly cytoplasmic, but during keratinocyte differentiation, nuclear retention is observed. This differential localization suggests that DINO has distinct functional roles in keratinocyte differentiation and HPV biology. Our findings highlight DINO as a lncRNA that promotes HPV genome replication and suggest that lncRNAs may play underappreciated roles in host-virus interactions. This work provides a foundation for further exploration of lncRNAs as potential therapeutic targets in HPV-associated diseases. IMPORTANCE Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are the causative agents of many anogenital tract and oral cancers, yet the host factors that trigger and support viral genome replication during the productive life cycle are incompletely understood. This study identifies the long non-coding RNA DINO as a host regulator that promotes HPV DNA replication, replication focus formation, and early viral gene expression independently of keratinocyte differentiation. We further show that DINO exhibits context-dependent subcellular localization, suggesting distinct functional roles in cellular stress responses and HPV biology. These findings reveal an underappreciated role for host lncRNAs in virus-host interactions and provide new insight into cellular pathways that support HPV genome replication.

papers.title_zh: lncRNA DINO 对 HPV 基因组 复制的分化独立激活。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) rely on multiple host cell factors to replicate the viral genome, yet the contribution of host long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to viral genome maintenance and amplification in the productive life cycle remains poorly understood. In this study, we show that the lncRNA damage-induced long non-coding RNA (DINO) is a driver of HPV DNA replication. DINO levels increase during keratinocyte differentiation, and ectopic expression of DINO promotes both HPV genome replication and the formation of replication foci, and this is independent of keratinocyte differentiation signals. Ectopic DINO expression increases select early viral transcript levels, including E1^E4, E1, and E2. Notably, DINO’s subcellular localization is also context-dependent: during DNA damage, DINO is predominantly cytoplasmic, but during keratinocyte differentiation, nuclear retention is observed. This differential localization suggests that DINO has distinct functional roles in keratinocyte differentiation and HPV biology. Our findings highlight DINO as a lncRNA that promotes HPV genome replication and suggest that lncRNAs may play underappreciated roles in host-virus interactions. This work provides a foundation for further exploration of lncRNAs as potential therapeutic targets in HPV-associated diseases. IMPORTANCE Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are the causative agents of many anogenital tract and oral cancers, yet the host factors that trigger and support viral genome replication during the productive life cycle are incompletely understood. This study identifies the long non-coding RNA DINO as a host regulator that promotes HPV DNA replication, replication focus formation, and early viral gene expression independently of keratinocyte differentiation. We further show that DINO exhibits context-dependent subcellular localization, suggesting distinct functional roles in cellular stress responses and HPV biology. These findings reveal an underappreciated role for host lncRNAs in virus-host interactions and provide new insight into cellular pathways that support HPV genome replication.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 依赖多种 宿主 细胞因子来复制病毒 宿主,但 宿主 长非编码 RNA (lncRNA) 对病毒 宿主 在生产生命周期中维持和扩增的贡献仍知之甚少。在这项研究中,我们证明 lncRNA 损伤诱导的长非编码 RNA (DINO) 是 HPV DNA 复制的驱动因素。DINO水平在角质形成细胞分化过程中增加,DINO的异位表达促进HPV 基因组复制和复制灶的形成,并且这与角质形成细胞分化信号无关。异位 DINO 表达会增加选定的早期病毒转录水平,包括 E1^E4、E1 和 E2。值得注意的是,DINO 的亚细胞定位也与环境相关:在 DNA 损伤期间,DINO 主要位于细胞质中,但在角质形成细胞分化过程中,观察到核保留。这种差异定位表明 DINO 在角质形成细胞分化和 HPV 生物学中具有独特的功能作用。我们的研究结果强调了 DINO 作为一种促进 HPV 基因组 复制的 lncRNA,并表明 lncRNA 在 宿主 与病毒相互作用中可能发挥着未被充分认识的作用。这项工作为进一步探索lncRNA作为HPV相关疾病的潜在治疗靶点奠定了基础。重要性 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是许多肛门生殖道和口腔癌的病原体,但在生产生命周期中触发和支持病毒 基因组 复制的 宿主 因素尚不完全清楚。这项研究将长非编码 RNA DINO 确定为 宿主 调节因子,可促进 HPV DNA 复制、复制焦点形成和独立于角质形成细胞分化的早期病毒基因表达。我们进一步表明 DINO 表现出上下文依赖性亚细胞定位,表明在细胞应激反应和 HPV 生物学中具有不同的功能作用。这些发现揭示了 宿主 lncRNA 在病毒-宿主 相互作用中未被充分认识的作用,并为支持 HPV 基因组 复制的细胞途径提供了新的见解。

papers.title: [Testicular Germ Cell Tumors and Penile Cancer: Molecular-Based Diagnosis and Treatment].
papers.abstract: Molecular diagnostics and targeted therapies are increasingly evolving towards a personalized medicine approach. This review summarizes recent advances in testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) and penile cancer, with a focus on emerging biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. Conventional serum tumor markers such as AFP, β-HCG, and LDH remain important but are limited by suboptimal sensitivity and specificity. Novel biomarkers, particularly microRNA miR-371a-3p, have demonstrated substantially higher diagnostic accuracy and may improve risk stratification, detection of disease recurrence, and treatment decision-making in TGCTs. In addition, the analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising liquid biopsy procedure. In penile squamous cell carcinoma, molecular classification based on human papillomavirus (HPV) status and comprehensive genomic profiling are becoming increasingly relevant for prognosis and therapeutic selection. The identification of actionable molecular alterations has facilitated the development of immunotherapy, anti-EGFR strategies, and antibody-drug conjugates. Early clinical data also suggest that ctDNA may provide valuable information for treatment monitoring and early relapse detection. Despite these promising findings, further prospective studies and standardized methodologies are required before many of these approaches can be incorporated into routine clinical practice. Overall, these developments highlight the ongoing transition towards biomarker-driven precision oncology and the potential for more individualized management of patients with TGCTs and penile cancer.

source_records.title: Testikuläre Keimzelltumoren und Peniskarzinom – Molekularbasierte Diagnostik und Therapie
source_records.abstract: Zusammenfassung Die molekulare Diagnostik und Therapie urologischer Tumoren entwickelt sich zunehmend hin zu einer personalisierten Medizin. Der vorliegende Übersichtsartikel beleuchtet aktuelle Entwicklungen bei testikulären Keimzelltumoren (TGCT) und dem Peniskarzinom mit besonderem Fokus auf innovative Biomarker und zielgerichtete Therapiekonzepte. Bei TGCT weisen klassische Serumtumormarker wie AFP, β-HCG und LDH nur eine begrenzte Sensitivität und Spezifität auf. Neue Biomarker, insbesondere die MicroRNA miR-371a-3p, zeigen dagegen eine deutlich höhere diagnostische Genauigkeit und ermöglichen eine verbesserte Risikoabschätzung, Rezidiverkennung und Therapieplanung. Darüber hinaus gewinnt die Analyse zirkulierender Tumor-DNA (ctDNA) als Liquid-Biopsy-Verfahren an Bedeutung. Beim Peniskarzinom spielen die molekulare Klassifikation anhand des HPV-Status sowie genomische Analysen eine zunehmend wichtige Rolle. Die Identifikation therapeutisch relevanter Alterationen eröffnet neue Möglichkeiten für Immuntherapien, Anti-EGFR-Strategien und Antibody-Drug Conjugates. Erste Studien zur ctDNA zeigen zudem ein großes Potenzial für Therapiemonitoring und Früherkennung von Rezidiven. Trotz vielversprechender Ergebnisse sind weitere prospektive Studien und standardisierte Verfahren erforderlich, bevor viele dieser Ansätze in die klinische Routine integriert werden können. Insgesamt verdeutlichen die aktuellen Entwicklungen den Wandel hin zu einer biomarkerbasierten Präzisionsmedizin in der Uroonkologie.

papers.source_body_en: Molecular diagnostics and targeted therapies are increasingly evolving towards a personalized medicine approach. This review summarizes recent advances in testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) and penile cancer, with a focus on emerging biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. Conventional serum tumor markers such as AFP, β-HCG, and LDH remain important but are limited by suboptimal sensitivity and specificity. Novel biomarkers, particularly microRNA miR-371a-3p, have demonstrated substantially higher diagnostic accuracy and may improve risk stratification, detection of disease recurrence, and treatment decision-making in TGCTs. In addition, the analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising liquid biopsy procedure. In penile squamous cell carcinoma, molecular classification based on human papillomavirus (HPV) status and comprehensive genomic profiling are becoming increasingly relevant for prognosis and therapeutic selection. The identification of actionable molecular alterations has facilitated the development of immunotherapy, anti-EGFR strategies, and antibody-drug conjugates. Early clinical data also suggest that ctDNA may provide valuable information for treatment monitoring and early relapse detection. Despite these promising findings, further prospective studies and standardized methodologies are required before many of these approaches can be incorporated into routine clinical practice. Overall, these developments highlight the ongoing transition towards biomarker-driven precision oncology and the potential for more individualized management of patients with TGCTs and penile cancer.
papers.abstract_zh: 分子诊断和靶向治疗正日益向个性化医疗方法发展。本综述总结了睾丸生殖细胞肿瘤(TGCT)和阴茎癌的最新进展,重点关注新兴生物标志物和靶向治疗策略。传统的血清肿瘤标志物,如 AFP、β-HCG 和 LDH 仍然很重要,但受到敏感性和特异性欠佳的限制。新型生物标志物,特别是 microRNA miR-371a-3p,已证明具有更高的诊断准确性,并且可以改善 TGCT 中的风险分层、疾病复发检测和 Z​​XQTERMVQXZ 决策。此外,循环肿瘤 DNA (ctDNA) 的分析已成为一种有前途的液体活检方法。在阴茎鳞状细胞癌中,基于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 状态的分子分类和全面的基因组分析与预后和治疗选择变得越来越相关。可操作的分子改变的鉴定促进了免疫疗法、抗 EGFR 策略和抗体药物偶联物的发展。早期临床数据还表明,ctDNA 可能为 治疗 监测和早期复发检测提供有价值的信息。尽管有这些有希望的发现,但在将其中许多方法纳入常规临床实践之前,还需要进一步的前瞻性研究和标准化方法。总体而言,这些进展凸显了向生物标志物驱动的精准肿瘤学的持续转变,以及对 TGCT 和阴茎癌患者进行更个体化管理的潜力。

papers.title: Therapeutic resistance in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: molecular mechanisms, clinical challenges, and precision strategies
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) exhibits exceptional sensitivity to chemoradiotherapy, with 5-year overall survival exceeding 80%, thereby providing a compelling rationale for treatment de-escalation. However, 15%–20% of patients develop therapeutic resistance and locoregional recurrence, resulting in markedly inferior outcomes. This Review systematically dissects the molecular architecture of treatment resistance in HPV-positive OPSCC, with particular emphasis on mechanisms conferring resistance to radiotherapy, platinum-based chemotherapy, and EGFR-targeted therapy (cetuximab). We delineate core drivers — aberrant DNA damage response (DDR) signaling, epigenetic reprogramming, cancer stem cell (CSC) plasticity, and non-coding RNA networks—and pinpoint actionable vulnerabilities. The contributions and limitations of patient-derived organoids, genetically engineered mouse models, and pivotal clinical trials (notably RTOG 1016) are critically appraised. We address persistent controversies, including the complex relationship between de-escalation and resistance, and highlight the lack of integrative resistance biomarkers. Finally, we propose a roadmap to bridge translational gaps and accelerate the development of precision strategies that circumvent resistance.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on therapeutic resistance in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), examining molecular mechanisms, clinical challenges, and precision strategies to address resistance to chemoradiotherapy, platinum-based chemotherapy, and EGFR-targeted therapy.

papers.title_zh: HPV 阳性口咽鳞状细胞癌的治疗耐药:分子机制、临床挑战和精准策略
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) exhibits exceptional sensitivity to chemoradiotherapy, with 5-year overall survival exceeding 80%, thereby providing a compelling rationale for treatment de-escalation. However, 15%–20% of patients develop therapeutic resistance and locoregional recurrence, resulting in markedly inferior outcomes. This Review systematically dissects the molecular architecture of treatment resistance in HPV-positive OPSCC, with particular emphasis on mechanisms conferring resistance to radiotherapy, platinum-based chemotherapy, and EGFR-targeted therapy (cetuximab). We delineate core drivers — aberrant DNA damage response (DDR) signaling, epigenetic reprogramming, cancer stem cell (CSC) plasticity, and non-coding RNA networks—and pinpoint actionable vulnerabilities. The contributions and limitations of patient-derived organoids, genetically engineered mouse models, and pivotal clinical trials (notably RTOG 1016) are critically appraised. We address persistent controversies, including the complex relationship between de-escalation and resistance, and highlight the lack of integrative resistance biomarkers. Finally, we propose a roadmap to bridge translational gaps and accelerate the development of precision strategies that circumvent resistance.

papers.title: Evolution of hazard of recurrence and death after surgery for oropharyngeal cancer according to HPV status.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-related oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is associated with improved survival compared with HPV-negative disease. However, limited evidence is available on how the risk of recurrence and cancer-related death evolves according to HPV status. METHODS: This multicentre retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent upfront surgery with neck dissection for OPSCC between 2010 and 2022. HPV status was determined by p16 immunohistochemistry. Overall survival, cancer-specific survival, disease-free survival, and disease-free specific survival were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Time-varying hazard rates (HR) for cancer-related death, local recurrence, regional recurrence, distant metastasis, and secondary primary tumor were estimated over a five-year period using nonparametric smoothed hazard functions, stratified by p16 status. RESULTS: Among 650 patients, 284 (43.7%) had p16-positive tumours. Cancer-related mortality peaked during the second postoperative year in both groups, but occurring earlier and at markedly higher levels in p16-negative than in p16-positive patients (15 vs 18 months; annual HR: 12.7% vs 4.1%). Local and regional recurrence risks were the highest within the first two years, remained significantly higher and more prolonged in p16-negative patients than in p16-positive counterpart. The risk of second primary tumors was higher for p16-negative patients than p16-positive ones, remaining almost constant during follow-up in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: The risk of recurrence and cancer-related death after surgery for OPSCC differs in magnitude and in timing according to p16 status. Hazard function analysis provides clinically relevant information beyond conventional survival estimates and may support time-adapted follow-up strategies and patient counselling in OPSCC.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This multicentre retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent upfront surgery with neck dissection for OPSCC between 2010 and 2022.
analysis_en.methods: HPV status was determined by p16 immunohistochemistry. Time-varying hazard rates (HR) for cancer-related death, local recurrence, regional recurrence, distant metastasis, and secondary primary tumor were estimated over a five-year period using nonparametric smoothed hazard functions, stratified by p16 status.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 650 patients, 284 (43.7%) had p16-positive tumours.
